items.reason: Guardian circuit breaker selects the cyber policy (consecutive=1, recent=1) when the turn model's catalog specialty is cyber, interrupting the turn after one denial; standard thresholds are unchanged (Rust f141dc77f0, #37190).

PathURI equality and containment are ASCII-case-insensitive for Windows-convention paths (decoded identity bytes), while hosts stay exact and POSIX paths remain case-sensitive; percent-encoded native separators fail closed (Rust 4cb8676d3a, #37129).

Registering the built-in tool_search first removes namespace tools whose namespace is tool_search, preventing them from sharing the search tool's model-visible surface; other namespaces are preserved and a plain-name duplicate still errors (Rust 98da2c4499, #37188).

The image_resize_notice feature flag (disabled by default) and the ImageResizeNotice developer fragment with Rust's exact message format are implemented; Go's image prep validates and re-encodes data URLs without actual dimension-changing resizes, so no notices are emitted in practice until Go performs real resizing (Rust fa5d5ae047, #37134).

Streamable HTTP MCP handshakes track a remaining initialization deadline (context deadline or StartupTimeout) and apply it to initialize, notifications/initialized, and server/discover requests, clearing it once the handshake finishes so later executor calls are unaffected (Rust e244a9d94e, #37168).

Go EnvironmentManager tracks provisioned Noise environments across registration with pending/ready/failed states (Rust f5345f1ee8, #37147): RegisterDeferredNoiseEnvironment returns a registration handle whose Ready completion publishes capability roots and whose failure or abandonment is terminal; MaterializePendingNoiseEnvironment and ReportProvisioningStatus keep the same record from Pending through Ready or Failed (report-before-materialization creates it), reports are idempotent while Ready<->Failed transitions are rejected, ordinary environments ignore reports and conflict with materialization (ProvisioningModeConflict), and Status/Info defer connection until provisioning succeeds (Status returns pending without dialing; ready then dials; failed surfaces the first error).

thread/settings.update now persists the active permission profile and runtimeWorkspaceRoots, and prepareTurnStartParams applies them to future turns (explicit turn-start values win) while the active turn keeps its immutable snapshot. Go resolves the effective permission profile and workspace roots fresh per turn, so a profile update lands in the next turn's tool-router sandbox context without reconnecting environments; mirrors Rust 30d99232f4 (#37031).

view_image is a stable default-enabled feature; features.view_image=false removes the native image viewer from the turn tool surface (fresh subagents and guardian reviewers inherit the disabled viewer) while configured MCP tools stay available, and the Rust app-server v2 suite manifest now covers the module (Rust 78f00743f9, #36966).
wait/terminate host requests get a 60s transport allowance; on stall the connection is invalidated so the next execution reconnects (Rust 8e3b5d3e87).

ParseAgentPluginMCPConfig translates Agent Plugins v1 mcp.json into Codex MCP config: stdio/streamable-http normalization, PLUGIN_ROOT/PLUGIN_DATA expansion, contained paths, secure endpoints, client-owned header filtering, per-server errors (Rust bd12b3a9ec).

WithConfigOverrides stores base_instructions override into instructions_template and preserves other message fields; personality-disabled renders default personality into the template (Rust df72fdb415).
Generic plugin usage guidance is emitted only when the selected model has include_plugin_usage_instructions (Rust e4e0c7070e).

MCP servers can opt out of direct/deferred/code_mode surfaces via omit_tools_from; the per-server policy is applied when building the turn tool registry, tool exposures gained code_mode_only and deferred_model_only, deferred-model-only tools stay searchable but not nested-callable, and client-private _meta is stripped from MCP results surfaced to Code Mode (Rust 51c9ed6d4f).

rollout.Load and history/message-history lookup no longer fail on records beyond bufio.Scanner's default 64KB token limit (ReadBytes-based JSONL parsing and 16MB scanner buffers), so large embedded tool outputs and pasted prompts survive resume and thread lookup.

Approving an exec-policy amendment reports the newly saved command prefix to the model exactly once as 'Approved command prefix saved:' (sandbox.FormatAllowPrefixes mirrors Rust format_allow_prefixes) instead of re-injecting the full permissions text; drained per thread+turn post-tool (Rust 1bbfb5cfad).

The Go remote client negotiates the dual-websocket-v1 capability, opens the paired /bulk/{token} WebSocket when the host advertises it, routes delegate tool calls/results on the bulk lane while notifications and control traffic stay on the control lane, enforces per-socket message families, and rejects missing/unexpected pairing tokens (Rust 60c722e075).

runtimeutil.Budget.RecordUsage now charges provider-reported codex_rollout_budget_units directly (finite, non-negative or fatal error), falling back to weighted token accounting; mirrors Rust 8b8fa7276f (#36715).
Standard MCP catalog limit raised 1024->2048 and host-owned codex_apps (CodexAppsServerConfig) uses 8192 via per-server CatalogItemLimit; mirrors Rust e4e040881a (#36772).

Go exposes /fast only when fast_mode is enabled and the current model catalog contains a tier named fast. It toggles using that tier's actual ID versus default, persists the config alias fast, propagates the effective ID to local and remote turns, and reports persistence success/failure like Rust. Canonical /btw, /multi-agents, and /quit popup entries remain separate from aliases.

Rust /clear dispatches ClearUi, which starts a fresh session while keeping the previous rollout resumable. Go TUI and interactive command paths now reset thread identity, transcript, and idle status instead of only clearing visible messages.

Runtime-backed slash commands now execute real actions: /app launches the Codex Desktop thread deep link, /rollout reads the active thread rollout path, /sandbox-add-read-dir validates and adds a readable root, /import invokes external-agent detect/import RPCs, and /memories opens a dedicated settings modal with persisted memory edits.

Go validates and emits ordered initialItems notifications, stores codexResponseHandoffMode, and routes streamed assistant output from appserver turns into bounded realtime handoff_append itemAdded notifications. Commentary/final channels, final-message prefix, UTF-8-safe head/tail truncation, and client-managed/codexResponsesAsItems skips are covered.

Go rollout loading and doctor inventory now accept .jsonl.zst, map compressed siblings to canonical .jsonl state-DB keys, prefer plain rollouts, and report corrupt compressed files without false stale rows.
Go emits completion items directly from the active AgentLoopResult, which provides the same externally observable active-turn filtering without Rust's app-server notification backfill stage.

Go prepares model metadata and permission requirements locally before TUI startup, so the Rust parallel remote requests have no Go-side latency or scheduling counterpart; startup behavior is already equivalent.

Go detects external project Markdown memory, verifies SHA-256 content, imports under extension-scoped resources with scope.json and source/project/cwd/hash metadata, rejects path/hash failures, and removes resources for disappeared projects without inventing rollout provenance.
The Rust change removes an internal crate only; Go's realtime wire behavior remains covered and unchanged.

Linux Landlock/bwrap is verified on a native Kali runner. Native Windows platform and production ConPTY gates pass. Forty-seven relevant packages compile for Darwin/arm64, and Darwin network/sandbox vet plus actionlint pass. The macOS workflow now directly tests Keychain roots, a Unix-socket HTTP round trip, native seatbelt enforcement, and desktop/platform behavior; a native macOS workflow artifact is still required.

The opt-in Windows cancellation diagnostic still fails on Rust bbbf396839: Rust leaves the PowerShell descendant alive and the resumed turn aborts, while Go terminates the tree and resumes safely. Closing this requires an upstream Rust fix; Go must not regress process-tree safety to imitate the defect.
